title: Stanford's CS Curriculum
source: Mann's picks from the Stanford CS courses on the map — not the department's requirements
blurb: Algorithms, probability, linear algebra, parallel systems, numerical methods, AI.

steps.note: Roughgarden. Divide and conquer, sorting, graphs — the half of algorithms you use every day.
Probability written for programmers, and the prerequisite everything on the ML side assumes.
Boyd's applied linear algebra. Stanford's own courses point at Math 51 here, which is not online.
The systems course on this route. Parallel hardware and how to write for it — take it whenever.
The second half: greedy, dynamic programming, and what to do when a problem turns out to be NP-hard.
Numerical methods for graphics, vision and robotics. Worth it if you are heading near any of those.
AI the broad way — search, logic, planning — before CS229 narrows it to learning from data.
Machine learning, and where this route runs into Stanford's AI Curriculum.
Text, search and information retrieval. It stands on its own — no arrow, because nothing here is its prerequisite.
